newsitem.title: FRANCE: Talks resume in French truckers strike.
newsitem.headline: Talks resume in French truckers strike.

text.p: Negotiations resumed on Wednesday between striking French truck drivers and employers as ministers expressed optimism that an agreement in the 10-day-old dispute that has choked French highways could be reached within hours.
Truck drivers' unions, employers and government mediator Robert Cros resumed their talks at 4.45 p.m. (1545 GMT) with the issues of pay and working hours still to be resolved.

In a 20-hour overnight session which ended earlier on Wednesday, union and government officials said they had made substantial progress on two of the truckers' key demands, retirement at 55 instead of 60 and shorter working hours.

"We are pursuing our efforts on the pay issue so that we can quickly reach an agreement," Transport Minister Bernard Pons, who has been following the talks for the government, told the National Assembly at question time.
"We are making progress and we are on the verge of ending the crisis," he said, adding that the interests of both haulage firms and their employees were important to the French economy.
But unions said several issues were outstanding and they maintained their 218-roadblock stranglehold on French highways, which has led to fuel rationing and closed factories in some regions.
